title: Greedy
short: Make the best-looking choice at each step and never look back.
what: A greedy algorithm builds the answer one step at a time and always takes the option that looks best right now. It never undoes a choice, so it is fast. The catch: it only gives the right answer when the problem has a rule that makes the local best also the global best.
analogy: Paying cash at a shop: you hand over the biggest note that fits, then the next biggest, without planning ahead.

when: Pick the most, the least or the earliest at each step
Scheduling: fit the most meetings or jobs
You can argue a local choice never hurts later
python:
def make_change(amount, coins):
    picked = []
    for c in sorted(coins, reverse=True):  # biggest first
        while amount >= c:
            amount -= c
            picked.append(c)
    return picked
print(make_change(68, [25, 10, 5, 1]))
print(make_change(6, [1, 3, 4]))  # greedy: 3 coins, best is 3 + 3
watch: Greedy can be wrong. Test a tricky case, like coins 1, 3, 4 for 6, before trusting it.
If a choice can ruin later options, you probably need dynamic programming.
Most greedy solutions start with a sort; pick the sort key carefully.
